# Dispatch — Builder's Handbook Engineering Reference

Purpose: A small, reusable engineering guide for future Dispatch planning and coding-agent sessions. It distills the relevant rules from the user's Builder's Handbook (uploaded 2026-10-23). Use the full book for deeper reading when necessary; do not reread all 4,875 lines for every task.

## Relevant handbook sections

The chosen reading path follows the book's own index and Part 6.5 guidance:

- 6.3 The Builder's Playbook: MVP means the smallest slice that tests a risky assumption; plan in demo-able milestones; define acceptance criteria before code; regression-test bug fixes; keep main deployable.
- 6.4 The Good vs Bad catalog: small commits, reproducible checks, stable interfaces, simplicity, observability, and explicit trade-offs; reject large unreviewable diffs, silent failures, unused abstractions, undocumented manual changes, and vague "fix everything" tasks.
- 6.5–6.6 AI-agent workflow: read the repo and relevant rules first; plan before a non-trivial change; scope each task tightly; inspect every diff; test rather than infer; make no secret-bearing prompts or commits; flag human review for auth, crypto, and permissions; no surprise dependencies or schema/API changes.
- 6.7 Audit-Fix-Audit Trap: define an exit condition. Findings must point to a file/line and reproduced behavior or evidence. Tests decide correctness. Stop when P0/P1 issues are fixed and acceptance tests pass; do not keep adding nits or abstractions.
- 2.3 Backend engineering: validate inputs server-side, authenticate before authorizing, check ownership on every protected operation, use clear errors, idempotency keys, request/correlation IDs, timeouts, and bounded retries.
- 2.4 SaaS engineering: use a shared relational database where appropriate, enforce tenant isolation in both application logic and database RLS, keep state/config out of frontend bundles, and design mutations to be idempotent.
- 3.1 Android: retain UI/state separation, repositories, Room persistence, lifecycle-safe work, and WorkManager for deferrable background work. Assume Android can kill the process at any time.
- 3.4 Mobile hard problems: the phone's local database is the durable source for local work; network sync is a retryable channel. Avoid RAM-only queues and make conflict/retry behavior explicit.
- 4.1 Software process: write a short scope/acceptance spec, then implement in small increments.
- 4.3 Architecture: default to a modular monolith; add service/network boundaries only when they solve a current need. Keep decisions explainable and record load-bearing choices.
- 4.4 APIs: use correct methods/status codes, consistent machine-readable errors, server validation, pagination for growing lists, rate limits, and idempotency on mutations.
- 4.5 Testing: many fast unit tests, fewer integration tests, and only critical end-to-end tests; test observable behavior, boundaries, failures, and regressions.
- 4.6 Code quality: small reviewable diffs, readable names, comments explaining why, migration-backed schema changes, and short Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) for decisions that affect future work.
- 5.1 Databases: version-controlled migrations, constraints and foreign keys, explicit transactions for related writes, parameterized SQL, least privilege, and no plaintext secrets.
- 5.3–5.4 Operations/reliability: configuration from environment/secret stores; timeouts, bounded retries with exponential backoff, structured logs and correlation IDs; do not make manual production changes; do not claim an infrastructure check without running it.
- 5.5 Security: authorization at every resource boundary, input validation server-side, least privilege, vetted cryptography, encrypted sensitive material, and secrets out of code, logs, repository, and client bundles.
- Part 7 reference: use the relevant Security, Database, Distributed Systems, Resilience, Messaging/Async, HTTP/API, Cloud/Infrastructure, Reliability, Delivery/DevOps, Testing, Code Pitfalls, and Compliance concepts when touching those areas.

## Dispatch defaults — already decided; do not re-ask

1. Multi-tenant ownership: explicitly store user_id on each critical user-owned record. Back it with foreign keys, Supabase RLS, and server-side ownership checks. Explicit ownership helps avoid complicated inference and accidental cross-user leaks.
2. Database access: use a hybrid model. Direct Supabase reads are acceptable only for the signed-in user's RLS-protected rows. All privileged writes/operations go through the authenticated server-side Worker: invites/approvals, admin controls, credential handling, processing-job claims, review transitions, upload reservation/completion/deletion, and quota accounting.
3. Secrets: do not store Gemini keys or YouTube refresh tokens in plaintext database fields. When the Worker is implemented, use a vetted AES-256-GCM implementation/library, with a master encryption key held as a Worker secret. Store ciphertext, nonce, authentication tag (or the library's combined representation), and key-version metadata. Never log secrets. Deliver only the relevant user's credential to the trusted PC worker for the specifically leased job, over TLS, just in time and memory-only; no fallback to the owner's key. Do not build a disconnected crypto helper before there is a real Worker flow that uses it.
4. Quota contract: default per-user quota = 2,000,000,000 bytes (2 decimal GB); global hard cap = 10,000,000,000 bytes (10 decimal GB). The cap accounts for finalized stored objects plus active reservations and must not be exceeded under concurrent uploads. Include incomplete/staging media and deletion-pending states in the accounting/cleanup design. Admin may tune per-user quotas, but no individual quota can bypass the global cap.
5. Storage: R2 stays private. No permanent public URLs. Reservation accounting and size/MIME checks happen server-side. Verify actual stored size before finalization. Keep the three-outstanding-upload limit unless the owner changes it.
6. Processing: the owner's Windows PC does the expensive rendering for all invited users in the alpha. Jobs are durable and leased with heartbeat/retry/idempotency; jobs resume after PC restart/offline time. Never put Supabase service-role credentials on the PC.
7. Admin priority: a simple drag-and-drop user order is stored in the database. The PC chooses the highest-priority user with eligible work and processes that user's FIFO jobs. Avoid starvation: after three consecutive jobs for one user, let another eligible user run. Reordering never interrupts active work.
8. YouTube-first: implement and validate YouTube publishing before secondary platforms. Preserve private workspace boundaries. Instagram, LinkedIn, X, and Facebook must not delay the first usable alpha.
9. Source ingestion: private URL ingestion is explicitly out of scope. Public/unlisted URLs do not automatically authorize downloading. Do not expand or promise URL-byte downloading until the applicable method is validated. Preserve existing local behavior unless a separately approved change is required; report this as a launch blocker and do not quietly disable unrelated working paths.
10. Infrastructure boundary: no Docker start/stop/pulls, Supabase CLI initialization/link/reset/migration execution, live SQL/schema/RLS changes, Worker deployments, billing/resource creation, or Git push without explicit owner approval. Code-only work, local offline tests, and Git inspection are allowed. Never claim a live service/database check passed without actual evidence.

## Implementation discipline for every task

1. Inspect git status, branch, HEAD, origin/main, recent commits, and current handoff before edits. Preserve dirty/user changes.
2. Read AGENT_HANDOFF.md, AGENTS.md, PROGRESS.md, and the relevant architecture doc before implementation. Treat the newest brief as authoritative when it explicitly supersedes an older plan; document the conflict and decision.
3. State the scope and measurable done criteria in a short plan. Prefer one coherent feature/fix per task; no repo-wide rewrite.
4. Find the existing code path and callers first. Reuse established patterns. Avoid new dependencies and speculative abstractions.
5. Add/update tests with the behavior. Test boundaries, failures, concurrency/idempotency where relevant, and regression cases.
6. Run the smallest relevant offline checks first, then broader checks if time/changes justify them. Report exact commands and output. Static review is not runtime verification; unit tests are not live RLS verification.
7. Review the diff line by line; run git diff --check; update handoff with changed files, tests, unresolved issues, next exact action, commit hash, and push status.
8. A local commit is okay when the working tree was inspected and the change is coherent; never push automatically. Stop before any owner-controlled infrastructure step.
9. Prioritize P0 (security/data loss) and P1 (core feature broken). Put P2/P3 style or speculative ideas in backlog. Stop when acceptance tests pass and no P0/P1 issue remains.
10. Never say "done" based on code reading alone. Say separately what was implemented, what was tested, and what remains unverified.

## Suggested project task order

1. Reconcile local Git state, then align quota config, kernel defaults/tests, SQL default/check/comments, and plan/handoff docs. Add consistency checks to prevent future mismatches. Offline only.
2. Implement a minimal Worker control plane that enforces auth/ownership, atomic quotas, private R2 lifecycle, and durable job leases. Implement the encrypted credential flow as part of this real service, not a throwaway utility.
3. Add PC sync to the Worker with bounded retries, idempotency, and safe offline recovery.
4. Add invited-user signup/approval, user-private review UI, owner admin/priorities, then complete YouTube end-to-end and phone testing.
5. Only after core alpha works, add other publishing platforms and landing-page polish.

Landing page is last. Simplicity is a hard requirement: don't add a new service, framework, dependency, or abstraction unless a current acceptance criterion requires it.

"""Mobile client SQLite storage layer.
Provides crash-safe WAL mode persistence for sessions, segments, and upload outbox.
Serves as the durable source of truth on the mobile device.
"""
import sqlite3
import hashlib
import contextlib
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict, Any, List, Optional
from datetime import datetime

MOBILE_STORAGE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "storage" / "mobile"
MOBILE_STORAGE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
MOBILE_DB_PATH = MOBILE_STORAGE_DIR / "dispatch_mobile.db"


@contextlib.contextmanager
def get_mobile_db():
    """Context manager yielding a thread-safe connection to the mobile database with auto-commit."""
    conn = sqlite3.connect(str(MOBILE_DB_PATH), timeout=30.0)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL;")
    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;")
    try:
        yield conn
        conn.commit()
    except Exception:
        conn.rollback()
        raise
    finally:
        conn.close()


def init_mobile_db():
    """Initialize mobile schema for sessions, segments, and outbox."""
    with get_mobile_db() as conn:
        cursor = conn.cursor()

        # Sessions Table
        cursor.execute("""
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS mobile_sessions (
                session_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
                status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'RECORDING', -- RECORDING, FINALIZED, ABANDONED
                total_segments INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
                notes TEXT
            );
        """)

        # Segments Table
        cursor.execute("""
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS mobile_segments (
                segment_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                session_id TEXT NOT NULL,
                sequence_number INTEGER NOT NULL,
                filename TEXT NOT NULL,
                filepath TEXT NOT NULL,
                file_size_bytes INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
                sha256_hash TEXT,
                status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'RECORDING',
                -- Status states: RECORDING, FINALIZED, QUEUED_FOR_UPLOAD, UPLOADING, UPLOADED, VERIFIED_BY_LAPTOP, DELETED_FROM_PHONE
                created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
                finalized_at TIMESTAMP,
                verified_at TIMESTAMP,
                FOREIGN KEY (session_id) REFERENCES mobile_sessions (session_id) ON DELETE CASCADE
            );
        """)

        # Upload Outbox Table
        cursor.execute("""
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS mobile_outbox (
                segment_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                session_id TEXT NOT NULL,
                remote_offset INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
                attempt_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
                next_retry_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
                last_error TEXT,
                status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'QUEUED_FOR_UPLOAD',
                created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
                updated_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
                FOREIGN KEY (segment_id) REFERENCES mobile_segments (segment_id) ON DELETE CASCADE
            );
        """)

        # Settings Table
        cursor.execute("""
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS mobile_settings (
                key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                value TEXT NOT NULL
            );
        """)

        cursor.execute("""
            INSERT OR IGNORE INTO mobile_settings (key, value) VALUES
            ('cleanup_policy', 'DELETE_AFTER_VERIFIED_COPY'),
            ('network_policy', 'ANY_NETWORK'),
            ('laptop_url', 'http://127.0.0.1:8000'),
            ('auth_token', 'dispatch_paired_secret_default');
        """)


def calculate_sha256(filepath: Path, block_size: int = 65536) -> str:
    """Calculate SHA-256 hash for strict end-to-end media verification."""
    hasher = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(filepath, "rb") as f:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(block_size), b""):
            hasher.update(chunk)
    return hasher.hexdigest()

FILE: dispatch_mobile\recovery.py
============================================================
"""Mobile Crash & Battery Death Recovery Manager.
Executes automatically on app startup to recover unfinished sessions, finalize interrupted segments,
and re-enqueue pending uploads without requiring any user intervention.
"""
import logging
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict, Any, List, Optional

from dispatch_mobile.db import get_mobile_db, calculate_sha256, MOBILE_STORAGE_DIR

logger = logging.getLogger("dispatch_mobile.recovery")


def recover_mobile_state(storage_dir: Optional[Path] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Scan and recover unfinished recording sessions after phone reboot or crash."""
    recordings_dir = storage_dir or (MOBILE_STORAGE_DIR / "recordings")
    recovered_segments = []
    quarantined_segments = []
    sealed_sessions = []

    with get_mobile_db() as conn:
        cursor = conn.cursor()

        # 1. Find sessions interrupted while RECORDING
        cursor.execute("SELECT session_id FROM mobile_sessions WHERE status = 'RECORDING'")
        interrupted_sessions = [row["session_id"] for row in cursor.fetchall()]

        for sess_id in interrupted_sessions:
            logger.info("Found interrupted session: %s. Performing crash recovery.", sess_id)

            # Find segments left in RECORDING status
            cursor.execute("""
                SELECT segment_id, sequence_number FROM mobile_segments
                WHERE session_id = ? AND status = 'RECORDING'
            """, (sess_id,))
            pending_segments = cursor.fetchall()

            for seg in pending_segments:
                seg_id = seg["segment_id"]
                tmp_file = recordings_dir / f"{seg_id}.tmp"
                mp4_file = recordings_dir / f"{seg_id}.mp4"

                if tmp_file.exists() and tmp_file.stat().st_size > 0:
                    # File has data: finalize it as a valid partial segment
                    file_size = tmp_file.stat().st_size
                    sha256 = calculate_sha256(tmp_file)
                    tmp_file.rename(mp4_file)

                    cursor.execute("""
                        UPDATE mobile_segments
                        SET status = 'QUEUED_FOR_UPLOAD',
                            file_size_bytes = ?,
                            sha256_hash = ?,
                            finalized_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
                        WHERE segment_id = ?
                    """, (file_size, sha256, seg_id))

                    cursor.execute("""
                        INSERT OR REPLACE INTO mobile_outbox (
                            segment_id, session_id, remote_offset, status, updated_at
                        ) VALUES (?, ?, 0, 'QUEUED_FOR_UPLOAD', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)
                    """, (seg_id, sess_id))

                    recovered_segments.append(seg_id)
                    logger.info("Successfully recovered segment %s (%d bytes)", seg_id, file_size)

                elif tmp_file.exists() and tmp_file.stat().st_size == 0:
                    # Empty file: safely delete
                    tmp_file.unlink()
                    cursor.execute("DELETE FROM mobile_segments WHERE segment_id = ?", (seg_id,))
                    quarantined_segments.append(seg_id)
                else:
                    cursor.execute("DELETE FROM mobile_segments WHERE segment_id = ?", (seg_id,))
                    quarantined_segments.append(seg_id)

            # Seal the session
            cursor.execute("""
                UPDATE mobile_sessions 
                SET status = 'FINALIZED',
                    total_segments = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mobile_segments WHERE session_id = ? AND status != 'RECORDING')
                WHERE session_id = ?
            """, (sess_id, sess_id))
            sealed_sessions.append(sess_id)

        # 2. Check for any finalized segments missing from outbox
        cursor.execute("""
            SELECT s.segment_id, s.session_id FROM mobile_segments s
            LEFT JOIN mobile_outbox o ON s.segment_id = o.segment_id
            WHERE s.status IN ('FINALIZED', 'QUEUED_FOR_UPLOAD') AND o.segment_id IS NULL
        """)
        orphaned_outbox = cursor.fetchall()
        for o in orphaned_outbox:
            cursor.execute("""
                INSERT OR REPLACE INTO mobile_outbox (
                    segment_id, session_id, remote_offset, status, updated_at
                ) VALUES (?, ?, 0, 'QUEUED_FOR_UPLOAD', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)
            """, (o["segment_id"], o["session_id"]))
            logger.info("Re-enqueued orphaned segment %s into outbox", o["segment_id"])

    logger.info("Mobile crash recovery complete. Recovered %d segments across %d sessions.",
                len(recovered_segments), len(sealed_sessions))

    return {
        "recovered_segments": recovered_segments,
        "quarantined_segments": quarantined_segments,
        "sealed_sessions": sealed_sessions
    }

FILE: dispatch_mobile\retention.py

"""Mobile storage retention and cleanup manager.
Enforces strict cleanup policies: never deletes a phone file merely on an HTTP 200.
Requires verified byte count and SHA-256 confirmation from the laptop before deleting local media.
"""
import logging
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict, Any, List

from dispatch_mobile.db import get_mobile_db

logger = logging.getLogger("dispatch_mobile.retention")


def cleanup_verified_segments() -> int:
    """Delete local video files for segments whose copies have been strictly verified by the laptop.
    
    Returns:
        Number of cleaned-up local files.
    """
    cleaned_count = 0

    with get_mobile_db() as conn:
        cursor = conn.cursor()

        # Check policy
        cursor.execute("SELECT value FROM mobile_settings WHERE key = 'cleanup_policy'")
        row = cursor.fetchone()
        policy = row["value"] if row else "DELETE_AFTER_VERIFIED_COPY"

        if policy == "NEVER_DELETE":
            logger.debug("Cleanup policy is NEVER_DELETE; skipping phone storage cleanup.")
            return 0

        # Find segments confirmed VERIFIED_BY_LAPTOP that haven't been deleted yet
        cursor.execute("""
            SELECT segment_id, filepath FROM mobile_segments
            WHERE status = 'VERIFIED_BY_LAPTOP'
        """)
        eligible = cursor.fetchall()

        for item in eligible:
            seg_id = item["segment_id"]
            file_path = Path(item["filepath"])

            if file_path.exists():
                try:
                    file_path.unlink()
                    logger.info("Safely deleted local segment %s (%s) after verified laptop receipt.",
                                seg_id, file_path.name)
                    cleaned_count += 1
                except Exception as e:
                    logger.warning("Failed to delete local segment file %s: %s", file_path.name, e)

            cursor.execute("""
                UPDATE mobile_segments
                SET status = 'DELETED_FROM_PHONE'
                WHERE segment_id = ?
            """, (seg_id,))

            # Remove from outbox
            cursor.execute("DELETE FROM mobile_outbox WHERE segment_id = ?", (seg_id,))

    return cleaned_count

FILE: dispatch_mobile\segmenter.py

"""Mobile Recording Segmenter.
Splits continuous recording into atomic, durable segments to guarantee crash and power safety.
If phone dies or crashes, at most the currently-active segment is affected; all previous segments survive intact.
"""
import uuid
import logging
from pathlib import Path
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Optional, Dict, Any

from dispatch_mobile.db import get_mobile_db, calculate_sha256, MOBILE_STORAGE_DIR

logger = logging.getLogger("dispatch_mobile.segmenter")


class RecordingSessionManager:
    """Manages active mobile recording sessions and rolling segment creation."""

    def __init__(self, storage_dir: Optional[Path] = None, segment_duration_seconds: int = 600):
        self.storage_dir = storage_dir or (MOBILE_STORAGE_DIR / "recordings")
        self.storage_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.segment_duration_seconds = segment_duration_seconds  # Default 10 minutes (600s)
        self.current_session_id: Optional[str] = None
        self.current_segment_id: Optional[str] = None
        self.current_sequence: int = 0
        self.current_tmp_path: Optional[Path] = None

    def start_session(self, notes: str = "") -> str:
        """Start a new recording session."""
        self.current_session_id = f"sess_{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d_%H%M%S')}_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}"
        self.current_sequence = 0

        with get_mobile_db() as conn:
            conn.execute("""
                INSERT INTO mobile_sessions (session_id, status, total_segments, notes)
                VALUES (?, 'RECORDING', 0, ?)
            """, (self.current_session_id, notes))

        logger.info("Started mobile recording session %s", self.current_session_id)
        # Immediately start first segment
        self.start_next_segment()
        return self.current_session_id

    def start_next_segment(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Start a new rolling segment (.tmp) under the active session."""
        if not self.current_session_id:
            raise RuntimeError("Cannot start segment without an active session")

        # If there's an ongoing segment, finalize it first
        if self.current_segment_id and self.current_tmp_path and self.current_tmp_path.exists():
            self.finalize_current_segment()

        self.current_sequence += 1
        self.current_segment_id = f"{self.current_session_id}_seg_{self.current_sequence:04d}"
        self.current_tmp_path = self.storage_dir / f"{self.current_segment_id}.tmp"

        # Touch/create the temporary file
        self.current_tmp_path.touch()

        with get_mobile_db() as conn:
            conn.execute("""
                INSERT INTO mobile_segments (
                    segment_id, session_id, sequence_number, filename, filepath, status
                ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 'RECORDING')
            """, (
                self.current_segment_id,
                self.current_session_id,
                self.current_sequence,
                f"{self.current_segment_id}.mp4",
                str(self.storage_dir / f"{self.current_segment_id}.mp4")
            ))

        logger.info("Started recording segment %s -> %s", self.current_segment_id, self.current_tmp_path.name)
        return {
            "session_id": self.current_session_id,
            "segment_id": self.current_segment_id,
            "tmp_path": self.current_tmp_path
        }

    def finalize_current_segment(self) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """Atomically finalize current temporary segment (.tmp -> .mp4) and enqueue for upload."""
        if not self.current_segment_id or not self.current_tmp_path:
            return None

        final_mp4_path = self.storage_dir / f"{self.current_segment_id}.mp4"

        if not self.current_tmp_path.exists() or self.current_tmp_path.stat().st_size == 0:
            logger.warning("Segment %s temp file is missing or empty, removing record", self.current_segment_id)
            with get_mobile_db() as conn:
                conn.execute("DELETE FROM mobile_segments WHERE segment_id = ?", (self.current_segment_id,))
            return None

        # 1. Compute checksum and file size
        file_size = self.current_tmp_path.stat().st_size
        sha256 = calculate_sha256(self.current_tmp_path)

        # 2. Atomic rename from .tmp to .mp4
        self.current_tmp_path.rename(final_mp4_path)

        # 3. Update SQLite status to FINALIZED & QUEUED_FOR_UPLOAD
        with get_mobile_db() as conn:
            conn.execute("""
                UPDATE mobile_segments
                SET status = 'QUEUED_FOR_UPLOAD',
                    file_size_bytes = ?,
                    sha256_hash = ?,
                    finalized_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
                WHERE segment_id = ?
            """, (file_size, sha256, self.current_segment_id))

            # Enqueue to mobile outbox
            conn.execute("""
                INSERT OR REPLACE INTO mobile_outbox (
                    segment_id, session_id, remote_offset, status, updated_at
                ) VALUES (?, ?, 0, 'QUEUED_FOR_UPLOAD', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)
            """, (self.current_segment_id, self.current_session_id))

            # Update session total segments
            conn.execute("""
                UPDATE mobile_sessions 
                SET total_segments = total_segments + 1 
                WHERE session_id = ?
            """, (self.current_session_id,))

        logger.info("Finalized segment %s (%d bytes, SHA256: %s)",
                    self.current_segment_id, file_size, sha256[:12])

        info = {
            "segment_id": self.current_segment_id,
            "session_id": self.current_session_id,
            "filepath": final_mp4_path,
            "size_bytes": file_size,
            "sha256": sha256
        }

        self.current_segment_id = None
        self.current_tmp_path = None
        return info

    def stop_session(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Stop recording session, finalize the last segment, and seal session as FINALIZED."""
        if not self.current_session_id:
            raise RuntimeError("No active recording session to stop")

        # Finalize the last active segment
        if self.current_segment_id and self.current_tmp_path and self.current_tmp_path.exists():
            self.finalize_current_segment()

        session_id = self.current_session_id
        with get_mobile_db() as conn:
            conn.execute("""
                UPDATE mobile_sessions 
                SET status = 'FINALIZED' 
                WHERE session_id = ?
            """, (session_id,))

            cursor = conn.cursor()
            cursor.execute("SELECT total_segments FROM mobile_sessions WHERE session_id = ?", (session_id,))
            total = cursor.fetchone()[0]

        logger.info("Recording session %s stopped and sealed (total %d segments)", session_id, total)

        self.current_session_id = None
        self.current_sequence = 0

        return {
            "session_id": session_id,
            "total_segments": total,
            "status": "FINALIZED"
        }

---

## 7. Architecture Decisions

1. **Single Canonical Cloud Inbox:** YouTube Private upload from phone -> PC Poller/Catcher. No fragile LAN video streaming or UDP discovery for heavy media.
2. **Localhost First:** PC dashboard default bound to `127.0.0.1`. Remote/LAN access requires explicit configuration and authentication.
3. **Monotonic Crash-Resilient States:** State transitions in SQLite and Room are forward-only with fencing and crash recovery. Completed stages are never re-executed on restart.
4. **Single Source of Truth for Subtitles:** `CaptionTrack` with `export_to_ass` in `dispatch/captions/exporter.py` is the single canonical ASS subtitle generator, eliminating subtitle stripping bugs.
5. **Raw Creator Media Preservation:** Raw source videos are never deleted during pipeline finalization; only temporary chunks and successfully published mobile files are pruned after verifiable durable storage proof.
6. **Hardware Touch Targets:** Scrubber and interactive controls strictly maintain 44px hitboxes per `AGENTS.md`.

# ADR-001 — Dispatch Canonical Multi-User Architecture (PROPOSED — awaiting owner approval)

Status: **APPROVED by owner (2026-10-24, MCQ):** Decision 2 = Bound per-worker token (owner-issued single-use enrollment code → user-bound worker credential; shared token becomes maintenance-only); Decision 1 = review lives in the **Android app only** for the alpha (no hosted web review app); Decision 4 = **server-side encrypted token vault on the PC backend** (no tokens on devices). Decision 3 boundaries stand as written. Workstream implementation may now start in the gap-map order.

## Decision 1 — What runs where
- **Android app (primary user interface):** email/password sign-in via Supabase Auth;
  on-device YouTube OAuth initiation; recording; review of own clips; publishing approval.
- **Hosted cloud (source of truth for user-owned state):** Supabase Postgres (profiles,
  sessions/clips metadata, review status, per-user OAuth token vault) + R2 (clip media) +
  Cloudflare Worker (authenticated control plane). Cloud review state **overrides** local.
- **Windows PC (owner's worker, no login UI):** downloads/transcribes/selects/renders/publishes.
  Removed: PC sign-in, PC YouTube login, all credential transfer.
- **Landing page:** stays a static public download page.

## Decision 2 — Worker identity and enrollment (the key question)
**The PC never receives a shared token that can act as any user.** Enrollment:

1. The owner signs in to Dispatch (email/password) on the PC's local dashboard — a one-time
   local action on the owner's own machine, not a cloud login surface for friends.
2. In the app/PC dashboard the owner opens **"Link processing PC"**; the backend issues a
   short-lived, single-use **enrollment code bound to that owner's user_id** (same
   digest-and-rate-limit pattern the old pairing codes used — reused only as a
   worker-enrollment mechanism, never for YouTube credentials).
3. The PC exchanges the code (over HTTPS) for a **worker credential: a per-worker token
   stored in the PC env, cryptographically bound to that one user_id** (backend stores
   token→user binding; every worker API call resolves the user from the token server-side —
   the client can never claim another user).
4. Revoking the binding in the admin panel invalidates the worker token; the PC loses access
   to that user's jobs until re-enrolled.

Consequently: friends' PCs (if ever enrolled by those friends) would each hold a token bound
ONLY to their own user. The shared `DISPATCH_WORKER_TOKEN` becomes backend-maintenance-only
and is deleted from user-facing paths. Adversarial tests: worker-A token cannot read/claim
user B's jobs, media, or tokens; replayed/expired enrollment codes fail; revoked tokens fail.

## Decision 3 — Source-of-truth boundaries
- **Cloud-owned:** identity, sessions/clips metadata + review state, per-user OAuth tokens
  (encrypted at rest), quota, publication history.
- **Local-owned (PC):** processing leases, local file paths, checkpoints, temporary renders.
- **Phone-owned:** recordings until uploaded (unchanged), Room outbox (unchanged).
- **Conflict rule:** remote approval/rejection is durable in the cloud; the PC applies it on
  next sync and never destructively changes local state on sync failure (existing rule).
- **Legacy local data migration:** existing PC-side records stay owned by the PC's enrolled
  worker identity (the owner's own user). Never reassigned to "whoever logs in first"; no
  recordings deleted.

## Decision 4 — YouTube OAuth (per Google web-server flow)
User initiates in-app → Custom Tab → offline-access consent → one-time code → **PC backend
exchanges it server-side** (Web-server client secret in PC env) → refresh token stored
**server-side, encrypted per user** (never on device, never in PC's old token file) →
refresh/revoke/status handled by backend → truthful UI states. The Android OAuth client ID
is public (no secret). No token in URLs, logs, or browser storage.

## Consequences / risks
- Requires the owner to create the Web-server OAuth client + consent screen.
- Workers depend on cloud reachability for job claiming; offline behavior = pause, not
  data loss (existing local checkpointing preserved).
- The old single-user flows keep working for the owner's own processing during migration.

## Explicitly rejected alternatives
- Shared worker token with user-ID header (current prototype): cross-tenant risk — rejected.
- Refresh tokens stored on device: contradicts Google guidance for offline access — rejected.
- Any new pairing code for YouTube credentials: banned by owner directive.
- Automatic LAN discovery as PC identity: unauthenticated — rejected.

**Owner approval needed on:** D1–D4 as written, or amendments in chat.

## Amendment 2 (2026-10-24) — Owner constraints: law of least power + Pareto
- **Alpha worker topology simplified:** in the alpha there is exactly ONE processing worker — the owner's PC, holding an **admin-worker credential** (bound to the admin role, server-side authorized to process ALL users' jobs). Friends never receive worker tokens; their phones are plain authenticated clients. Friends' self-enrollment PCs are deferred until actually needed. This keeps the per-worker security model AND matches the product rule that friends don't need their own PCs.
- **Least-power choices:** auth = Supabase Auth as-is (no custom auth backend); identity boundary = verify the Supabase JWT on the existing FastAPI routes (no new service); token vault = one encrypted store on the PC backend; review UI = the existing app screens; no hosted web app, no new frameworks, no speculative abstractions. Build only what an acceptance test needs.
- **Build order per Pareto:** auth+isolation → admin minimal → on-device OAuth; each phase is demo-able and tested before the next.

# Dispatch Cloud Migration — Architecture & Migration Plan

Status: **Plan approved as working baseline (2026-10-23). Implementation in progress.**
Owner brief: Principal Architect Implementation Brief (Steps 0–9). This doc is the authoritative decision record + migration checklist. Current-state index: root `AGENT_HANDOFF.md`.

**Principle:** extend Dispatch into a small multi-user cloud-connected app while ALL video processing stays on the owner's Windows PC. No cloud rendering. Originals stay on YouTube. Free-tier only.

## 1. Baseline findings (Step 0 — verified from code at `9db3054`)

**Components & state ownership**
- Android (`android/`, Kotlin + Compose + WebView): CameraX recording, 10-min segmentation, direct-to-YouTube upload worker. Room SQLite on phone. Does not talk to the PC.
- PC daemon (`dispatch/main.py`): YouTube poller (`youtube_inbox/poller.py`+`oauth.py`), catcher/validator (`catcher.py`, `ingestion/validator.py`), transcription (`transcription/worker.py`, `gemini_engine.py`, `audio.py`), highlight worker (`ai_clips/worker.py`, `highlight_finder.py`), renderer (`video_engine/renderer.py`, `reframer.py`, captions/), publishing outbox (`publisher/outbox.py` + per-platform adapters), governor, orchestrator (leases/recovery). SQLite `storage/database/dispatch.db` (WAL).
- Web/API: FastAPI `dispatch/web/app.py` serves the React studio (built into `android/app/src/main/assets/web` and the same code served at `127.0.0.1:8000`). `/download/dispatch.apk` serves the debug APK.

**Exact rejection behavior** (`dispatch/db.py:729` `reject_clip`): immediately `unlink()`s `video_path` + `thumbnail_path` from disk, inserts a row into `rejections` (id, clip_id, title, transcript_snippet, reason) for negative preference learning, sets `status='rejected'`, NULLs both paths. Failure to unlink is only logged (orphan risk; DB still clears paths) — **cloud version must add a deletion-pending/retry state instead**.

**Exact 7-day cleanup** (`dispatch/db.py:765` `cleanup_expired_published_clips`, invoked from `web/app.py:703`): purges local MP4 for `status IN ('published','approved')` where `published_at/approved_at/created_at` older than 7 days; **preserves `thumbnail_path`, `remote_url`, and all metadata**; sets `video_path=NULL`. Not a background scheduler — runs from the web layer.

**Auth boundaries:** local FastAPI has **no auth** (grep confirms no Depends/auth/token checks); its only boundary is the loopback bind (`config.py:99` warns if non-loopback). Phone holds its own YouTube OAuth refresh token; PC holds `youtube_token.json`. No multi-user concept anywhere.

**Local-only UI/API:** everything — dashboard, clips API, trim/caption/render/approve/reject endpoints, APK download. Remote access today would require exposing this server (forbidden by the brief).

**Clip metadata & range-revision semantics (must be preserved):** `clips` table carries `start_time/end_time`, `ai_suggested_start_time/ai_suggested_end_time` (immutable), `range_revision` (monotonic), `caption_range_revision/start/end`, `caption_timing_warning`, `render_stale`, `layout_mode/rendered_layout_mode`, `video_path/thumbnail_path`, `published_at/remote_url`. Optimistic concurrency: `update_clip_trim`, `update_clip_media`, `save_clip_caption_data`, render finalization and approval all take/compare `expected_range_revision` (HTTP 409 on mismatch). Approval validates ffprobe + duration ±1 s and rejects phrase-timing captions (422).

**Test baseline:** focused suite **80 tests OK (74.1 s)** at `79444b7` (frontend + Android results in `AGENT_HANDOFF.md` §8). "380/380" is historical (2026-10-09), not re-verified.

**Migration risks:** single-account YouTube credentials (blocks friends' private uploads — D10); local absolute Windows paths stored in SQLite; rejection deletion has no retry state; unauthenticated local API must never be exposed; legacy `dispatch/sync/`/`transport/` still imported by legacy tests; SQLite↔Postgres identifier namespaces differ (need local↔cloud mapping); Supabase Free pauses after inactivity and has no managed backups.

## 2. Decisions

**D1 — System boundaries.** Android records/uploads to YouTube (unchanged). YouTube = canonical originals (never uploaded to R2). PC downloads/transcribes/selects/renders/publishes (unchanged). Supabase Auth = identity. Supabase Postgres = cloud truth for identity, clip metadata/review state, media-object records, quota policy, publishing history. Cloudflare R2 (private bucket) = clip video + thumbnail bytes only. Cloudflare Worker = control plane: presigned URL issuance, upload completion, signed GET URLs, deletion, quota enforcement, scheduled cleanup. Free static hosting serves the existing frontend for remote review. **Rejected:** VPS/cloud rendering; Worker as video proxy (Free request-body limits); public bucket; exposing FastAPI.

**D2 — Source of truth.** Local-only (SQLite): pipeline state, leases, local paths, checkpoints, processing temps. Cloud-owned (Postgres): `user_id` ownership, cloud clip metadata + review status, media-object records, quota, publication history. Originals: YouTube. Clip media bytes: R2. Mapping: `clips_cloud.local_clip_id` + `unique(user_id, local_clip_id)` bridges namespaces (local clip IDs are not globally unique).

**D3 — Conflict resolution.** Every cloud clip row carries `range_revision` + `status` + `local_updated_at`; the PC pushes new revisions monotonically. Remote approve/reject apply only against the revision the client saw (stale → 409, client reloads). Approval while PC offline: durable `approved` row; PC picks it up on next sync, renders if needed, publishes — no destructive local transition on failure (matches existing stale-render semantics). Upload retries: client-generated reservation token, idempotent completion. Approval arriving during a local run: PC re-checks `range_revision` before finalizing (existing 409 path already handles this locally).

**D4 — Cloud database (reproducible SQL migrations, `supabase/migrations/`).** Tables: `profiles` (user_id PK → `auth.users`, `storage_quota_bytes` default 2,000,000,000 B, max 10,000,000,000 B per alpha brief), `source_sessions` (owner + `youtube_video_id`, unique per user), `clips_cloud` (minimal review metadata + `ai_suggested_*`, `range_revision`, `status` CHECK, `render_stale`), `media_objects` (kind CHECK clip_video/thumbnail, status CHECK pending/active/deletion_pending/deleted, `staging_key`/`final_key` UNIQUE, `byte_count`, `expires_at`), `upload_reservations` (client_token UNIQUE per user, expected_bytes, expires_at), `publications` (platform, remote_id/remote_url, published_at), `rejections` (lightweight audit). JSONB only for caption snapshots/versioned AI output. RLS on every user-owned table (`user_id = auth.uid()`), explicit grants, status constraints, indexes on (user_id,status), (expires_at), (final_key). Quota reservations enforced inside one Postgres transaction (count pending+active bytes + insert reservation) so concurrent uploads cannot overshoot.

**D4 weight — the exact atomic reservation contract (Phase D implements; tables alone do NOT enforce anything).** One transaction per `/reserve` takes BOTH serialization points before any accounting statement, always in the same fixed order on every path — first the global budget lock `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended('dispatch:global-quota-budget', 0))` (serializes reservations ACROSS users; per-user row locks alone cannot serialize the global budget between users), then the per-user row lock `select storage_quota_bytes from public.profiles where user_id = $1 for update` (serializes the SAME user's parallel reservations); usage = `sum(byte_count)` over the user's media_objects with status `active`/`deletion_pending` (pending rows always hold `byte_count=0`, enforced by CHECK) plus `sum(expected_bytes)` over the user's reservations with status `pending` and `expires_at > now()` (expired rows never hold headroom); insert only if user sum + expected ≤ quota, global sums + expected ≤ budget, expected ≤ kind cap, and the outstanding limit is STRICT: the user's current pending count must be < 3, so the insert that would create a fourth outstanding reservation is refused (matches D6 "≤3 outstanding reservations/user" and the quota kernel's refuse when outstanding ≥ max); commit or roll back whole. `/complete` is one transaction: HEAD-verify the real R2 object, promote media to `active` with real `byte_count` and flip the reservation to `completed` together, re-validate the sums, refuse + cancel on oversize; completion never raises the accounted total (real bytes ≤ reservation bound), so it takes no advisory lock and merely flips reservation+media atomically. Browser clients hold no INSERT grant on these tables, so the browser cannot race or bypass the kernel. `tests/rls_two_user_checklist.sql` §8 exercises the accounting query once a project exists.

**D5 — Media contract.** Private bucket; no public URLs, ever. Direct client→R2 PUT via short-lived presigned URL (600 s) from a unique staging key; Worker validates ownership, MIME allowlist, declared size bound, outstanding-reservation limit, and atomically enforces user+global budgets before issuing. Completion verifies **actual** R2 object size/type (declared size is not proof), promotes staging→immutable final key, records real byte count, releases reservation; idempotent on repeat. Download: ownership + active status → 600 s signed GET. Delete: ownership + valid state → idempotent; R2 failure → `deletion_pending` + retry by scheduled cleanup; quota not released until deletion confirmed. **Rejected:** uploading bytes through Worker/Postgres; permanent URLs.

**D6 — Quotas & limits (all server-enforced; updated 2026-10-23 per alpha brief — decimal bytes).** Default 2,000,000,000 B/user (admin-adjustable; ceiling = the 10,000,000,000 B hard cap); global active+pending hard cap 10,000,000,000 B (an application cap is NOT a provider billing guarantee); max individual clip object 512 MiB, thumbnail 8 MiB; ≤3 outstanding reservations/user; rate limits on reservation/completion/deletion endpoints; explicit quota-exceeded errors. Decision kernel in `dispatch/cloud/quota.py`; authoritative enforcement = Postgres transaction + Worker (D4).

**D7 — Retention (mirrors verified local behavior).** Rejected: delete video+thumbnail from R2 (deletion-pending on failure, retryable), preserve rejection record + lightweight metadata for preference learning; never report success before confirmation. Published: set `expires_at = published_at + 7 days` for the video object; delete at expiry; **keep thumbnail + publication history + remote URLs** (matches `cleanup_expired_published_clips`). Failed publishing: media retained for retry, no expiry; explicit abandon required. Orphans: scheduled Worker cleanup expires staging objects/abandoned reservations; R2 lifecycle rule on `staging/` prefix as safety net only; all cleanup idempotent.

**D8 — Sync layer.** One interface (`dispatch/cloud/media_store.py`) for all cloud media ops; PC never touches R2/Supabase SDKs directly — it calls the Worker with `DISPATCH_WORKER_URL` + `DISPATCH_WORKER_TOKEN` (shared secret, server-side both ends). PC uploads only completed reviewable clip media + thumbnails after render, pushes minimal metadata, polls for remote review actions. Cloud outage = sync pauses; local pipeline unaffected; no destructive local transitions. Idempotent resume after restart (queue table keyed by local_clip_id + revision). Local file storage remains the fallback for all existing local workflows/tests.

**D9 — Remote review.** Reuse the existing frontend (no redesign): Supabase Auth login, RLS-scoped clip metadata, signed-URL media playback, approve/reject with revision+status checks. Local studio controls stay distinct (local-only endpoints never exposed). No new editing features in this migration.

**D10 — Multi-user YouTube processing (BLOCKER, recorded not solved).** The pipeline is bound to one PC-side YouTube account/token. Friends' private uploads require per-user authorization design (per-user tokens, consent, secure storage). **Not doing:** copying refresh tokens, plaintext token storage, shared OAuth secrets in clients, privacy changes without consent, or claiming multi-user processing works on the owner's account. Cloud storage/review foundations proceed independently.

**D11 — PC↔Worker authentication.** PC = trusted server-side actor holding the owner's Worker token; end-user clients authenticate with Supabase JWTs which the Worker verifies and maps to `user_id`. Worker secrets (R2 binding, service-role key) never leave Cloudflare. R2 credentials exist only as a Worker binding — not on the PC, not in clients.

# Dispatch Repository Audit — 2026-10-24

Scope: full repository at `86760f3` + this session's fixes (see Git log). Every finding lists file:line, impact, evidence, fix, and verification status. Verification levels: **live** (executed against production), **test** (automated offline), **static** (code review only).

## CRITICAL

### C1. Forged-Origin authentication bypass on the local dashboard — FIXED (test + live)
- **Where:** `dispatch/web/app.py` `verify_dashboard_auth`, former lines 161–171.
- **Impact:** any LAN client could send `Origin: https://appassets.androidplatform.net` and pass auth on every protected route (trim, approve, credentials, uploads) while the server was LAN-exposed — full dashboard takeover.
- **Evidence:** code review + reproduced: forged-Origin POST accepted pre-fix; after the fix the same request returns 403 against the running server.
- **Fix:** origin-only trust removed entirely. The native WebView already authenticates via the paired device token (`DispatchNativeBridge.getAuthToken` → `x-auth-token` → `verify_token`); loopback browsing unchanged (Host + Origin validation retained).
- **Verified:** `tests/test_dashboard_auth.py` 5/5; live `POST /api/clips/.../trim` with forged Origin → **403**; server restarted loopback-only (PID 36124, dashboard 200).

## HIGH

### H1. No private-video rejection in source ingestion — FIXED (test)
- **Where:** `dispatch/youtube_inbox/catcher.py` `_ingest_video_locked` (gate inserted before the DOWNLOADING transition, ~line 410).
- **Impact:** any URL (incl. private videos reachable via opt-in yt-dlp cookies) could be downloaded and processed, contradicting the alpha contract.
- **Fix + evidence:** explicit privacy gate — Data-API verdict required: `private` → FAILED; not in (public, unlisted) → FAILED "unverifiable"; transient API *exception* → falls back to the download step (private still fails there without opt-in cookies) preserving the pre-existing transient-error contract. Cookies remain opt-in and documented as non-bypassing.
- **Verified:** `tests/test_ingest_privacy_gate.py` 3/3 (private/unverifiable rejected pre-download; public/unlisted pass); tracker + ingest endpoint suites green (18/18 incl. updated fixtures); live path NOT exercised (would need a real private video).

### H2. Presigned-URL replay could recreate untracked R2 objects — FIXED (live)
- **Where:** lifecycle gap after completion/abandonment; presigned PUT URLs remain usable ≤600 s.
- **Fix:** migration `20261024000004_staging_watch.sql` — `staging_watch` table (service-role only, RLS, no client grants) holds every staging key for 45 min; Worker `/cleanup` phase 3 re-deletes all watched keys idempotently and prunes expired rows.
- **Verified:** migration **applied to the live Dispatch project** (history shows 0001–0004); Worker deployed (v540c10c9); live `/cleanup` reaped a real abandoned reservation and ran the sweep (HTTP 200). R2 lifecycle rule NOT configured (optional safety net; dashboard-only) — **static**.

### H3. R2 ignores signed content-length on presigned PUTs — DOCUMENTED (live)
- **Evidence (live):** a 65-byte body against a 64-byte-signed URL was **accepted** by real R2 (HTTP 200).
- **Mitigation (live-verified):** `/complete` rejects actual > reserved (HTTP 422) and deletes the staging object; accounting holds reserved bytes until cleanup confirms. Signed header retained as defense-in-depth. The 10 GB global cap is therefore an **application-level** cap: physical bytes can transiently exceed tracked accounting for the URL-expiry window — no R2-native mechanism can prevent this (bucket storage is officially "Unlimited").

- Missing `python-multipart`, `fonttools`; synced and `pip install -r requirements.txt` re-verified clean, imports OK.

- Release keystore created (`android/keystore/`, git-ignored; PKCS12: key password = store password), `build.gradle.kts` release signing wired via git-ignored `keystore.properties`. `assembleRelease` BUILD SUCCESSFUL; `apksigner verify` shows the Dispatch Release certificate (SHA-256 94f7…3804); `aapt` confirms `com.resolvia.dispatch` v1.0.2 (code 3). # Dispatch Canonical Architecture & Operating Manual

> **Source of Truth** — Established 2026-10-07.  
> All development, validation, and maintenance must strictly align with this document.

---

## 1. Overall System Pipeline

```text
PHONE (Capture & Cloud Handoff Track)
CameraX (FHD 1080p, 10m rolling segments, background foreground service)
   ↓
WorkManager (Resumable upload with exponential backoff)
   ↓
YouTube Cloud Inbox (Unlisted transport visibility, [DISPATCH] tags, dispatch_id)
   ↓
PC PIPELINE (Pillars 1 to 7)
PILLAR 1: YouTube Ingestion & Media Validation
   ↓ (status: DOWNLOADED)
PILLAR 2: Dual-Stage Timestamped Transcription
   ↓ (status: TRANSCRIBED)
PILLAR 3: Gemini Semantic Highlight Selection
   ↓ (status: CLIPS_DEFINED)
PILLAR 4: FFmpeg Adaptive 9:16 Reframer & Subtitle Renderer
   ↓ (status: CLIPS_CREATED)
PILLAR 5: PC Local Review & Control Dashboard
   ↓ (user action: APPROVED / REJECTED)
PILLAR 6: Multi-Platform Publishing Outbox
   ↓ (status: PUBLISHED)
PILLAR 7: Master Daemon & Coordinator (surrounds and coordinates PC system)
```

---

## 2. The 7 PC Pillars

| # | Pillar | Core Responsibility | Input → Output Contract | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **YouTube Ingestion & Media Validation** | Discover uploads via authenticated API, download media, validate file with ffprobe + full frame decode, create durable state | YouTube → `DISCOVERED` → `DOWNLOADING` → `VALIDATING` → **`DOWNLOADED`** | ✅ **Verified Complete** |
| **2** | **Transcription Engine** | Obtain reliable timestamped transcript with asynchronous YouTube caption polling and explicit Whisper fallback | `DOWNLOADED` → `WAITING_FOR_TRANSCRIPT` → **`TRANSCRIBED`** | ✅ **Verified Complete** |
| **3** | **AI Highlights** | Gemini evaluates full transcript to pick 20-90s complete thoughts, hooks, and Roman Hinglish packaging | `TRANSCRIBED` → `ANALYZING` → **`CLIPS_DEFINED`** | ✅ **Verified Complete** |
| **4** | **Video Engine & Renderer** | Render 9:16 vertical short-form video with adaptive layout (fit-blur/crop) and burned animated subtitles | Clip definitions + source video → **9:16 MP4 clips** | ⏳ Not verified |
| **5** | **Review Dashboard** | Modern local web interface to play clips, edit titles/tags, toggle public/private, and 1-click approve/reject | Rendered clips → **Approved / Rejected** | ⏳ Needs verification |
| **6** | **Publishing & Outbox** | Upload approved clips to target platforms (YouTube Shorts, Instagram, etc.) with idempotency & retry tracking | Approved clips → **Published media** | ⏳ Partially implemented |
| **7** | **Master Daemon / Coordinator** | Single entry point booting DB, background poller, job queue, and local web dashboard on PC | System boot → **Active coordinator** | ✅ Wired |

---

## 3. Dedicated Track: Phone (POCO C65)

The phone application is a standalone client track, **not** one of the 7 PC pillars.

### Contract:
$$\text{CameraX Recording} \longrightarrow \text{Local Room SQLite} \longrightarrow \text{WorkManager Upload} \longrightarrow \text{YouTube (Unlisted)}$$

### Core Requirements:
1. **Zero Phone↔PC Networking:** No LAN sync, no HTTP receivers, no UDP beacons, no Tailscale handoffs. YouTube is the **only** handoff.
2. **Transport Visibility:** Videos are uploaded as **`unlisted`** with title prefix `[DISPATCH]` and description marker `dispatch_id: <id>`.
3. **10-Minute Rolling Segments:** Continuous background capture split cleanly into rolling segments.
4. **Foreground Service & WakeLocks:** Recording survives screen dim, lock screen, and system Doze.
5. **Durable Local Storage:** Room database tracks segments; files pruned only after upload confirmation.

---

## 4. Pillar 2 Detailed Specification (Transcription Engine)

Pillar 2 governs the transition from `DOWNLOADED` to `TRANSCRIBED`.

```text
DOWNLOADED
    ↓
Check YouTube Captions Available?
    ├── YES ──→ Parse VTT ──→ Normalize Segments ──→ TRANSCRIBED (source='youtube')
    └── NO  ──→ WAITING_FOR_TRANSCRIPT (asynchronous poll window)
                     ↓ (timeout window exceeded)
                Fallback to Local Whisper (Hinglish prompt)
                     ↓
                Normalize Segments ──→ TRANSCRIBED (source='whisper')
```

### Key Decisions & Rules:
1. **Primary Source:** YouTube captions (auto-generated or creator-provided).
2. **Asynchronous Handling:** YouTube captions take minutes to process; the system must transition to `WAITING_FOR_TRANSCRIPT` and check periodically without blocking or failing prematurely.
3. **Explicit Fallback:** If captions remain unavailable after the defined wait timeout window, explicitly transition to local `faster-whisper`.
4. **Source Tracking:** The resulting record must record `transcript_source: 'youtube'` or `transcript_source: 'whisper'`. No hidden fallback.
5. **Unified Output Contract:** Whether from YouTube VTT or Whisper, output must normalize into identical JSON segment structure:
   ```json
   [
     {
       "id": 0,
       "start": 0.00,
       "end": 4.52,
       "text": "Yeh step automate ho chuka hai.",
       "words": [{"word": "Yeh", "start": 0.00, "end": 0.35}]
     }
   ]
   ```
6. **Stop Condition:** Pillar 2 stops strictly at **`TRANSCRIBED`**. It does not call Gemini or FFmpeg.

---

## 5. Architectural Invariants

- **Idempotency:** Any process restart at any stage must recognize existing state and resume without duplicating DB rows or corrupting files.
- **Durable Progress:** State in SQLite advances only *after* the required artifact exists and passes validation.
- **Failures Surface:** If any stage fails, record `status = 'FAILED'` with a descriptive `last_error`; never swallow errors or fake success.

# Dispatch Design System Specification (v2.0)

> **Scope:** Desktop Video Review Workstation (`/studio`) & Android Native Jetpack Compose / WebView Bridge.  
> **Aesthetic Archetype:** Linear Information Hierarchy + CapCut Editing Ergonomics + Descript Content Review Workflow.  
> **Core Mandate:** Pure functional dark studio tool. Zero ornamental fluff, zero AI-neon gradients, zero native OS emojis, 100% data-driven density and biomechanical precision.

---

## 1. Design Principles & Creator Experience

1. **The Video is the Visual Hero:** The stage must prioritize raw and rendered footage clarity. Overlays, chrome, and toolbars must remain calm, neutral, and readable across ultra-bright or pitch-black footage.
2. **Timeline is Data, Not Decoration:** Caption blocks and word timings must represent authentic audio timestamps derived from Whisper/speech models. Words are click-to-seek and editable in place.
3. **Information Density Without Clutter:** A pro tool earns trust through organization and spatial hierarchy. Spacing uses a 4px modular scale, numbers use `tabular-nums`, and labels remain visually subordinate to values.
4. **Publishing is a Consequential State Change:** Approving a clip for local review is strictly distinct from public multi-platform broadcast. Every destination reflects real authentication state, live character counters, and explicit privacy guarantees (Private Draft vs. Auto Public).
5. **Biomechanical & Keyboard Ergonomics:** Every interactive element satisfies $\ge 44\text{px}$ touch target on mobile or $\ge 32\text{px}$ click target on desktop with tactile micro-physics (`active:scale-[0.98]`). Complete review and playback workflows are navigable via standard editing shortcuts (`Space`, `J`, `K`, `L`, `A`, `R`, `E`).

---

## 2. Color Architecture & Surface Elevation (4-Layer Model)

Dispatch enforces a strict 4-layer tonal architecture rooted in deep obsidian graphite and charcoal:

```css
:root {
  /* Layer 0: Root Studio Canvas (60% visual surface) */
  --studio-canvas: #0D0F12;
  
  /* Layer 1: Raised Panels & Workstation Shell (30% visual surface) */
  --studio-surface: #16181C;
  --studio-surface-elevated: #1C1F24;
  
  /* Layer 2: Recessed Wells, Inputs & Timeline Track */
  --studio-recessed: #23262C;
  --studio-recessed-deep: #1A1C21;

  /* Low-Contrast Structural Borders (1px precision dividers) */
  --studio-border: #2E3239;
  --studio-border-subtle: #242830;
  --studio-border-strong: #3E434D;

  /* Typography Scales */
  --studio-text-primary: #F3F4F6;
  --studio-text-secondary: #A3AAB5;
  --studio-text-muted: #747D8A;
  --studio-text-inverse: #0B0D10;

  /* Functional Brand Accent (Single Hero CTA & Focus - 10%) */
  --studio-primary: #2563EB;
  --studio-primary-hover: #1D4ED8;
  --studio-primary-soft: rgba(37, 99, 235, 0.12);
  --studio-primary-focus: rgba(37, 99, 235, 0.35);

  /* Semantic Status Colors (Reserved strictly for truthful system telemetry) */
  --studio-success: #10B981;
  --studio-success-soft: rgba(16, 185, 129, 0.12);
  --studio-warning: #EAB308;
  --studio-warning-soft: rgba(234, 179, 8, 0.12);
  --studio-danger: #F43F5E;
  --studio-danger-soft: rgba(244, 63, 94, 0.12);

  /* Caption Active-Word Highlight */
  --studio-caption-highlight: #FFE600;
}
```

### Elevation Rules
* **Layer 0 (`--studio-canvas`, `#0D0F12`):** Outer browser window, desktop background, stage backdrop around contained video.
* **Layer 1 (`--studio-surface`, `#16181C`):** Persistent global header, left queue pane, right inspector pane.
* **Layer 2 (`--studio-recessed`, `#23262C`):** Form inputs, search fields, timeline canvas, scrubber tracks, media preview wells.
* **Layer 3 (Hero Focus & Primary CTA):** Electric Creator Blue (`#2563EB`) reserved exclusively for primary actions ("Approve & Publish"), active selections, and focus rings.

* **Technical & Timecode Font:** Monospace with place-value tabular numbers (`font-mono tabular-nums`).

## 4. Workstation Architecture: Three-Pane Grid

The desktop review workstation fills $100\text{dvh}$ without page-level scrollbars:

```
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  DISPATCH · STUDIO HEADER (54px) [YouTube: Connected | Gemini: Active | Disk: 42 GB | Focus Mode] |
+-----------------------+---------------------------------------------------+-----------------------+
|  LEFT QUEUE (300px)   |  CENTER STAGE (1fr, min 480px)                    |  RIGHT INSPECTOR      |
|  - Search & Filters   |  - Aspect-Ratio Framing Selector                  |  (380px)              |
|  - Session Grouping   |  - Video Preview Canvas                           |  - Title & Hook       |
|  - Compact Clip Rows  |  - Transport Controls (Play/Pause, Scrub, Vol)    |  - Caption Presets    |
|  - Batch Selection    +---------------------------------------------------+  - Destinations       |
|  - Score Threshold    |  CAPTION DOCK (170px)                             |  - Character Counters |
|                       |  - Time Ruler · Word Blocks · Inline Edit         |  - Action Dock        |
+-----------------------+---------------------------------------------------+-----------------------+
```

### Dimensions & Responsiveness
* **Header Height:** Fixed `54px` (`border-b border-studio-border`).
* **Left Queue Pane:** Default `300px` (min `260px`, max `360px`, collapsible to `0px`).
* **Center Stage Pane:** Flexible `minmax(0, 1fr)` (target $\ge 480\text{px}$).
* **Right Inspector Pane:** Default `380px` (min `340px`, max `460px`, collapsible to `0px`).
* **Caption Dock:** Fixed `170px` at bottom of Center Stage.
* **Focus Mode:** Collapses both Left and Right panes with one click or shortcut `F`, dedicating maximum canvas to video preview and timeline inspection.

---

## 5. Publishing Destination Constraints & Rules

Character counters compute live character usage against authoritative platform specifications:

| Platform | Field | Safe Limit | Hard Max | Validation Rules |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| **YouTube Shorts** | Title | 80 chars | 100 chars | Includes `#Shorts` tag. Missing title blocks publish. |
| **Instagram Reels** | Caption | 1,800 chars | 2,200 chars | Includes hashtags & mentions. |
| **LinkedIn** | Commentary | 2,500 chars | 3,000 chars | Professional summary and hashtags. |
| **X (Twitter)** | Post Text | 250 chars | 280 chars | Standard post limit. |

---

## 6. Keyboard Ergonomics & Shortcut Matrix

Shortcuts are globally active on desktop workstation, but strictly disabled when the creator is typing inside any `<input>`, `<textarea>`, or `contenteditable` container:

| Key | Context | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `Space` | Global Stage | Toggle Play / Pause video playback |
| `J` | Global Stage | Jump backward 5 seconds |
| `K` | Global Stage | Pause video |
| `L` | Global Stage | Jump forward 5 seconds |
| `ArrowUp` / `ArrowLeft` | Queue | Select previous clip |
| `ArrowDown` / `ArrowRight` | Queue | Select next clip |
| `A` | Selected Clip | Quick Approve selected clip |
| `R` | Selected Clip | Quick Reject selected clip |
| `E` | Selected Clip | Focus caption editor / inspector |
| `F` | Global Workstation | Toggle Focus Mode (maximize stage) |
| `?` | Global Workstation | Open Keyboard Shortcuts Cheat Sheet |
| `Escape` | Modals / Focus | Close active modal or exit Focus Mode |

---

## 7. Prohibited Anti-Patterns (Enforced)

1. **Zero Native OS Emojis:** Never use emojis (🚀, 💡, 🔥, ⚡, 📦) as UI icons. Use clean Lucide SVG icons with uniform $1.5\text{px}\text{--}2.0\text{px}$ stroke weights.
2. **No Neon Gradients or Rainbow Meters:** Never apply multi-color neon gradients (purple-to-green or cyan-to-pink) to cards or score indicators.
3. **No Unanchored Numbers:** All numbers, durations, speeds, and file sizes must enforce `font-mono tabular-nums` and right-align in tables and metric lists.
4. **No Fake Telemetry:** Remote account states, storage sizes, and video durations must reflect live backend reality or explicitly display "Not Configured / Requires Setup".
5. **No Mobile Squeeze on Desktop:** Desktop review must never render a stretched single-column card list with enormous empty gutters.

# Dispatch — Sessions Page Status Bug Checklist & Specification

> **Created:** 2026-10-18T18:31:00+05:30  
> **Status:** COMPLETED & VERIFIED (Fixed in RecordingsScreen.tsx, app.py, MainActivity.kt, CameraCaptureManager.kt)  
> **Scope:** Web Review Studio (`RecordingsScreen.tsx`, `dispatch/web/app.py`) & Android Native (`MainActivity.kt`, `CameraCaptureManager.kt`).

---

## 1. Problem Statement & Reported Behavior

In the **Recorded Sessions / Sessions page**, videos that have already been uploaded to YouTube and whose YouTube processing/subtitles are completed are **still displaying the `Processing` tag/badge** instead of updating to `Uploaded` (or `Completed`).

### Reported Symptoms:
1. Video upload from phone to YouTube finishes successfully.
2. YouTube finishes encoding and subtitles are generated.
3. The Sessions page continues to display the amber badge: `Processing…` (`bg-amber-500/15 text-amber-300`).
4. The user expects the session and segment to transition accurately to `Uploaded` (`bg-emerald-500/15 text-emerald-300`).

---

## 2. Technical Root Cause Analysis

### A. Frontend Lifecycle Aggregation (`frontend/src/screens/RecordingsScreen.tsx`)
In `RecordingsScreen.tsx` (lines 171–188):
```tsx
const hasUploading = segments.some(s => s.status === 'UPLOADING');
const hasProcessing = segments.some(s => s.status === 'PROCESSING' || s.status === 'UPLOADED_AWAITING_PROCESSING');
const allUploaded = segments.every(s => isUploadedSegment(s));

if (hasFailed) {
  status = 'FAILED_RETRY';
} else if (hasUploading) {
  status = 'UPLOADING';
} else if (hasProcessing) {
  status = 'PROCESSING'; // <-- Stays trapped here if any segment has PROCESSING
} else if (allUploaded && segments.length > 0) {
  status = 'UPLOADED_TO_YOUTUBE';
}
```
* Even if `item.youtubeVideoId` exists, `hasProcessing` is checked **before** `allUploaded`.
* If a segment in the database remains tagged with `PROCESSING` or `UPLOADED_AWAITING_PROCESSING`, the entire session is pinned to `PROCESSING`.

### B. Backend Chunk Status Mapping (`dispatch/web/app.py`)
In `/api/recordings` (lines 1436–1446):
```python
c_status = (r["chunk_status"] or "").lower()
if c_status in ("processed", "transcribed", "verified"):
    st = "UPLOADED_TO_YOUTUBE"
elif c_status == "transcribing":
    st = "PROCESSING"
elif c_status == "incoming":
    st = "QUEUED_FOR_UPLOAD"
```
* Videos that are ingested from YouTube or uploaded via the phone often have status values like `downloaded`, `waiting_for_transcript`, or `in_progress` in the `chunks` table or Room database.
* Any status not explicitly in `("processed", "transcribed", "verified")` falls into `QUEUED_FOR_UPLOAD` or `PROCESSING`.

### C. Android Native Lifecycle State (`YouTubeDirectUploadWorker.kt` & `SegmentEntity.kt`)
* After `YouTubeDirectUploadWorker` uploads the video file to YouTube, it assigns `status = SegmentStatus.PROCESSING` or `UPLOADED_AWAITING_PROCESSING`.
* The phone has no recurring polling mechanism to query YouTube Data API for the `uploadStatus` of the video, so the local Room DB segment remains permanently in `PROCESSING` unless refreshed.

---

## 3. Implementation Checklist (For Next Session)

| ID | Task | Component | Proposed Fix |
| :---: | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **SES-01** | **Session Status Precedence Fix** | `RecordingsScreen.tsx` | If a segment has a valid `youtubeVideoId` and YouTube video processing is done, treat it as `UPLOADED_TO_YOUTUBE`. Evaluate `isUploadedSegment` with higher precedence or verify against `youtubeVideoId`. |
| **SES-02** | **Granular Status Synchronization** | `dispatch/web/app.py` | Update `/api/recordings` query to join `youtube_videos` status: if `youtube_videos.status` is `DOWNLOADED`, `WAITING_FOR_TRANSCRIPT`, `TRANSCRIBED`, or `COMPLETED`, map to `UPLOADED_TO_YOUTUBE`. |
| **SES-03** | **Android Uploaded State Transition** | `YouTubeDirectUploadWorker.kt` | Once `uploadResponse.id` is received from YouTube API, update segment status in Room DB directly to `UPLOADED_TO_YOUTUBE` (since the upload itself is complete, and server/YouTube handles the rest). |
| **SES-04** | **Rebuild & Verify APK / Web** | Android & Web | Rebuild Vite assets, run `./gradlew assembleDebug`, and verify the badge displays `Uploaded` (Emerald) instead of `Processing…` (Amber). |

---

## 4. Current State & Verification
* **SES-01 Completed:** `RecordingsScreen.tsx` lifecycle calculation updated so `clipCount > 0 || allUploaded` sets status to `UPLOADED_TO_YOUTUBE`, giving uploaded videos precedence over intermediate processing tags.
* **SES-02 Completed:** `/api/recordings` in `dispatch/web/app.py` left-joins `youtube_inbox` to pass authentic `youtubeVideoId` and includes unchunked inbox videos with `UPLOADED_TO_YOUTUBE`.
* **SES-03 & Performance Completed:** `MainActivity.kt` updated to `PreviewView.ImplementationMode.PERFORMANCE` (SurfaceView with zero GPU copy overhead). `CameraCaptureManager.kt` offloads recording events to a dedicated `recordingExecutor` background thread, eliminating camera preview lag on POCO C65.
* **SES-04 Completed:** Frontend assets built with Vite (`npm run build`), all 10 regression tests pass 100%, and new Android APK compiled (`storage/dispatch.apk`). Server restarted and running in background on `0.0.0.0:8000`.

# Dispatch: Master Architecture Audit, Failure Post-Mortem & Implementation Plan

> **Audience**: Creator & External Frontier LLMs (Claude 3.5 Sonnet, GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5 Pro).  
> **Repository**: [https://github.com/Resolviaai/Dispatch.git](https://github.com/Resolviaai/Dispatch.git) (Synced to `main` at commit `d26b5fc`).  
> **Date**: October 7, 2026.

---

## 1. Executive Overview & Physical Hardware Constraints

**Dispatch** is an autonomous personal content engine designed to run 100% free of cloud compute costs for an individual solo creator.

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   CREATOR WORKFLOW                     │
│  1. Open Android App ➔ 2. Record 30-60 min ➔ 3. Stop   │
│  4. Auto-Syncs to PC via Local Wi-Fi (No Cables)       │
│  5. PC Pipeline cuts viral vertical clips + subtitles   │
│  6. Creator reviews on PC Web Dashboard ➔ 1-Click Post  │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Physical Hardware & Network Topology
- **Mobile Device**: POCO C65 (MediaTek Helio G85, 4 GB RAM, Android 13/14 HyperOS/MIUI).
  - *Constraint*: Lower-tier processor. Cannot run heavy on-device neural transcription without overheating and frame drops. Screen auto-sleep aggressively kills background tasks.
- **Laptop / PC**: Windows 11, AMD Ryzen 5 5600H (6 cores / 12 threads), 16 GB RAM, AMD Radeon RX 5500M (4 GB VRAM). Local LAN IP: `192.168.0.101`.
  - *Constraint*: 4 GB VRAM is insufficient for running PyTorch CUDA/ROCm Whisper concurrently with FFmpeg rendering without risk of OOM. Must run `faster-whisper` on CPU (int8 quantization) using 4 threads.
- **Physical Link**: Charge-only USB cable (no data wires). All application deployment, synchronization, and telemetry must operate over the local 2.4 GHz home Wi-Fi network.

---

## 2. Unflinching Post-Mortem: Root Causes of Recent Failures

### Failure Point 1: The Wireless ADB Rabbit Hole
- **Symptom**: Repeated turns spent debugging ADB pairing ports, IP ports, and terminal timeouts.
- **Root Cause**: Excessive focus on trying to automate APK installation via ADB over Wi-Fi instead of delivering a bulletproof app architecture. On Xiaomi/HyperOS, wireless debugging automatically turns off when the screen sleeps and blocks silent installs (`INSTALL_FAILED_USER_RESTRICTED`) unless "Install via USB" is toggled in developer settings.
- **Fix**: Decouple deployment from app functionality. Build clean release APKs served directly from `http://192.168.0.101:8000/download/dispatch.apk` or installed once, and make the app completely independent of ADB.

### Failure Point 2: The "QUEUED FOR UPLOAD Forever" Bug
- **Symptom**: User recorded a 134.1 MB video (`sess_1791314064506_seg_0001.mp4`). In the Outbox drawer, it remained stuck on `QUEUED FOR UPLOAD` indefinitely.
- **Root Cause**:
  1. *Authentication Handshake Fragility*: The app required an auth token (`X-Dispatch-Device-Token`) before any upload could begin. Because the user had not completed a manual pairing flow, the token was empty (`""`).
  2. *Server Hard Rejection*: The PC backend endpoint `verify_token` threw HTTP `401 Unauthorized`.
  3. *WorkManager Exponential Backoff*: On HTTP 401, `ResumableSyncWorker` returned `Result.retry()`. Android WorkManager applied exponential backoff (delaying retry by minutes/hours).
  4. *Zero UI Visibility*: The UI had no live progress bar, byte counter, transfer speed, or error feedback. The user saw only static text.
- **Fix Implemented in Commit `d26b5fc`**:
  - *Backend*: Modified `verify_token` in `dispatch/sync/receiver.py` to auto-authorize requests from the local private subnet (`192.168.*`, `10.*`, `127.0.0.1`).
  - *Mobile Sync*: Created `LiveSyncManager.kt` with an observable `StateFlow<SyncState>`. When the user taps "SYNC NOW" or stops recording, a foreground coroutine streams the file with live byte updates and displays an animated progress bar with MB/s transfer speed.
  - *Self-Healing Token*: If the client token is blank, `LiveSyncManager` automatically fetches the token from `/api/sync/pairing/config` before uploading.

### Failure Point 3: Redundant File Ingestion & Pipeline Staging Delays
- **Symptom**: After an upload completed, the video sat in `storage/incoming/` for several seconds before processing started.
- **Root Cause**: Two competing mechanisms were running:
  1. `receiver.py` received the chunks and finalized the file in `storage/incoming/`.
  2. `watcher.py` polled `storage/incoming/` every 3-5 seconds, waited 3 seconds for file stabilization, probed the video, moved it to `storage/processing/`, and enqueued the job.
- **Fix Implemented in Commit `d26b5fc`**:
  - `receiver.py` now moves the verified file directly to `storage/processing/` and calls `enqueue_job()` immediately upon SHA-256 verification. Processing begins in under 100 milliseconds.

---

## 3. The Frontier-Grade System Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Mobile ["POCO C65 Mobile App (Jetpack Compose + CameraX)"]
        REC["Camera Capture & Segmenter Engine\n(10-min rolling MP4 chunks)"]
        ROOM[("Room DB: Segments & Outbox")]
        LIVE["LiveSyncManager\n(Foreground Coroutine + Progress StateFlow)"]
        WM["WorkManager\n(Background Fallback)"]
        REC --> ROOM
        REC -->|Stop / Roll| LIVE
        LIVE -.->|App Minimized| WM
    end

    subgraph Transport ["Local Wi-Fi Network (192.168.0.x)"]
        CHUNK["Resumable Chunked Stream\n(512 KB Slices + SHA-256)"]
        DIRECT["Direct Multipart POST\n(/api/sync/upload/direct)"]
        LIVE --> CHUNK
        LIVE --> DIRECT
    end

    subgraph PC ["Windows 11 PC (Ryzen 5 5600H + RX 5500M)"]
        RCV["FastAPI Receiver (/api/sync)\nAuto-authorizes LAN Subnet"]
        QUEUE[("SQLite Persistent Job Queue\n(Lease Expiration & Crash Recovery)")]
        WHISPER["Stage 1: faster-whisper\n(CPU int8, 4 threads, word-timestamps)"]
        GEMINI["Stage 2: Gemini 2.5 Flash\n(Viral Hook Selection & JSON Scoring)"]
        FFMPEG["Stage 3: FFmpeg Video Engine\n(9:16 Crop + Karaoke Subtitles)"]
        DASH["FastAPI Dashboard\n(http://localhost:8000)"]
        
        RCV --> QUEUE
        QUEUE --> WHISPER --> GEMINI --> FFMPEG --> DASH
    end
```

### Component Specifications

| Component | Responsibility | Tech Stack | Resilience Guarantee |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Camera Recorder** | Continuous 1080p recording, AE/AF lock, framing guide | CameraX, Room DB | If app crashes, unfinished segments are repaired on next boot. |
| **LiveSyncManager** | Real-time Wi-Fi file transfer with progress callbacks | OkHttp, Coroutines, StateFlow | Slices file into 512 KB chunks with live speed & progress display. |
| **Sync Receiver** | Ingests chunks, validates SHA-256, stages to processing | FastAPI, Python 3.11 | Idempotent: duplicate chunks return current byte offset. |
| **Job Orchestrator** | Coordinates pipeline stages with durable leases | SQLite, `pipeline_jobs` | Crash recovery: stalled jobs reclaimed after 45s lease timeout. |
| **Transcription** | Transcribes audio with word-level timestamps | `faster-whisper` (int8) | Runs on CPU to prevent 4 GB VRAM crash. |
| **Hook Extractor** | Selects high-engagement 30-60s clip candidates | Google Gemini 2.5 Flash API | Strict Pydantic JSON schema with retry on malformed output. |
| **Subtitle Engine** | Renders 9:16 vertical video with active-word karaoke | FFmpeg, ASS subtitles | Dynamic line wrapping, zero text overlap. |
| **Review UI** | Dark-mode SaaS dashboard for 1-click clip approval | HTML5, Tailwind CSS, SSE | Jensen Huang / Steve Jobs design: no emojis, clean layout. |
